parsed.why: Statewide public-accommodation protections, gender-identity hate-crime penalties, accessible documents and a care shield materially improve the local picture. National document, entry and facility exposures still apply; local enforcement and shield scope are uncertain.

Statewide protections, a sanctuary law and a care shield offer meaningful local mitigation, though visitor coverage of the sanctuary is not established. Two recent killings are concerning but lack denominators; national restrictions remain operative.

The state adds school facility bans, a minor-present bathroom misdemeanour provision, sports exclusions and a restrictive care regime to the national exposures. These policies lower the score despite no documented local enforcement of the bathroom offence.

The state’s sex-based spaces policy and documented birth-sex custody placement—including assault followed by judicial dismissal of claims—add serious exposure to the national regime. Local document rules are mainly resident-facing and do not drive this rating.

Statewide protections, gender-neutral bathrooms, a care shield and repeal of a law used to harass trans people provide strong local mitigation. National border, document, facility and custody policies still apply; trans-specific social acceptance is undocumented.
